settings.consent.crash.body.value: If FinNative crashes, or signing in fails, it can send technical details that help find and fix the problem. Reports may include the signal, code addresses, thread information and device compatibility details, or which sign-in step failed and how the connection answered, plus a random crash report identifier, created when you turn this on and deleted when you turn it off or sign out, so that repeated crashes under one crash report identifier are counted once rather than once each. Whether each app session ended normally is also sent. They never include titles, Plex accounts, searches, server names or addresses, tokens, subtitle text, or the product analytics identifier.
settings.consent.crash.body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.consent.crash.body

settings.consent.product.body.value: FinNative can share which screens and features are used, how smoothly they respond, and broad sign-in and playback outcomes. Reports carry a random Analytics ID, created when you turn this on and deleted when you turn it off or sign out, and can include the app version, webOS version, television model and SoC, and whether a selected server is local, remote or relayed. They never include titles, Plex accounts, searches, server names or addresses, tokens, subtitle text, or exact viewing history.
settings.consent.product.body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.consent.product.body

settings.legal.privacy.plex_body.value: FinNative is an independent client for Plex. To sign you in, discover servers and provide Plex account features, the app communicates directly with Plex services. Plex processes information received by those services under Plex’s own Privacy Policy. FinNative’s developer does not receive that information.
settings.legal.privacy.plex_body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.plex_body

settings.legal.privacy.servers_body.value: To browse and play media, update watch progress and use server features, FinNative communicates directly with the Plex Media Servers you select. Those requests are handled by the selected server and its operator. FinNative’s developer does not receive them.
settings.legal.privacy.servers_body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.servers_body

settings.legal.privacy.local_body.value: FinNative stores your Plex account token and a separate token for each server you use. For every profile you have switched to on this television, it also keeps that profile's own server access token(s) and, for a PIN-protected profile, a one-way check computed from that PIN rather than the PIN itself. It also keeps the addresses and identifiers of those servers, the profile names and pictures on your account (pictures and other downloaded artwork are cached as bounded files for reuse across restarts), your Home library choices, your recent searches, your playback quality, Direct Play and app language preferences, and local technical logs: an event log and an error-output log, each emptied every time the app launches, a crash log that is kept until the television restarts, and a bounded storage status snapshot. It also stores your answers to the two optional-reporting questions, the random Crash report ID if you turned crash reports on, when the app session in progress started and was last active, the random Analytics ID if you turned product analytics on, any report waiting to be sent, and a marker recording how much of the crash log has already been read. It keeps no bookmark of its own for where you stopped watching: playback position is held by your Plex Media Server. Delete all local data in Settings signs out and removes FinNative data from this television.
settings.legal.privacy.local_body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.local_body

settings.legal.privacy.choices_body.value: Both optional reports are off until you turn them on, and either can be turned off again at any time in Settings. A one-off sign-in problem report is sent only when you press Send report. Delete all local data removes what FinNative stored on this television; it does not reach anything already sent. To ask what crash reports or product analytics hold for your installation, or to have them deleted, write to the contact below and quote your Crash report ID or Analytics ID from Settings, or the Report ID shown after a one-off report. Each identifier is the only handle its reports carry. Turning a category off deletes its identifier from this television, and so does signing out; reports already sent keep the old one, so copy it down first if you intend to ask for their deletion.
settings.legal.privacy.choices_body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.choices_body

settings.legal.privacy.processing_body.value: Optional crash reports are processed by Sentry in Germany and optional product analytics by PostHog in Germany. Plex processes what its own services receive under Plex’s Privacy Policy. A Plex Media Server you connect to may be located anywhere and is operated by whoever runs it, not by FinNative’s developer.
settings.legal.privacy.processing_body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.processing_body

settings.legal.privacy.uninstall_body.value: Removing FinNative removes the application, but webOS gives an application no way to run code as it is removed, so anything kept outside the application’s own directory can survive. Your sign-in is deliberately kept there so that reinstalling does not sign you out. Your optional-reporting answers and their Crash report ID and Analytics ID are kept with that sign-in, so that a decision you have already made is not put to you again after a reinstall. Your app language preference is also kept there. Use Delete all local data BEFORE uninstalling if you want nothing of FinNative left on this television.
settings.legal.privacy.uninstall_body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.uninstall_body

settings.playback.force_body.value:
Bypasses playback compatibility checks and always uses original quality. Playback may have no sound, display incorrectly, freeze, or crash the app. FinNative will not automatically switch to compatible playback and may not recover gracefully.

Enable this only if you understand these risks and know how to restart the app and return Direct Play to Auto.

settings.playback.direct_play.copy.value: Auto plays the original file when this television can; otherwise your server converts it. Disabled always converts. Force skips every check: for troubleshooting only.

settings.legal.privacy.plaintext_body.value: For a server you were asked about, FinNative also keeps whether you allowed an unencrypted connection on your home network, for the Jellyfin account that answered. Only the answer is stored. The permission itself is never stored and ends when a fresh check no longer reaches the same server address, at sign-in or sign-out, at a profile switch unless the new profile reaches that server at the same address, or when the app returns from the background.

settings.legal.privacy.fin.jellyfin_body.value: To sign you in, browse and play your media and keep your watch progress, FinNative talks only to the Jellyfin server you sign in to, and, while you sign in, looks for Jellyfin servers on your home network. It tells that server this app's name and version, the device name “LG TV” and a random device identifier, and reports what you play and how far you got, so the server can keep your progress and list this television among its devices. Those requests are handled by the server and whoever runs it, under their own terms. FinNative's developer does not receive them.
settings.legal.privacy.fin.jellyfin_body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.fin.jellyfin_body

settings.legal.privacy.fin.local_body.value: FinNative stores the address and identifier of your Jellyfin server and the access token the server issued when you signed in, never your password. It also keeps your Home library choices, your recent searches, the audio and subtitle tracks you picked for each show, your playback quality, Direct Play and app language preferences, downloaded artwork cached as bounded files for reuse across restarts, and local technical logs: an event log and an error-output log, each emptied every time the app launches, a crash log that is kept until the television restarts, and a bounded storage status snapshot. It keeps no bookmark of its own for where you stopped watching: playback position is held by your Jellyfin server. Delete all local data in Settings signs out and removes FinNative data from this television.
settings.legal.privacy.fin.local_body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.fin.local_body

settings.legal.privacy.fin.reports.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.fin.reports

settings.legal.privacy.fin.reports_body.value: FinNative sends no crash reports, analytics or other data to its developer or to anyone else. Apart from the requests to your Jellyfin server described above, nothing leaves this television, and its logs stay on it.
settings.legal.privacy.fin.reports_body.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.fin.reports_body

settings.legal.privacy.fin.retention_bod.value: Signing out removes your sign-in, your Jellyfin server's address and token, and the cached artwork. Your app language preference belongs to this television and is kept when you sign out. The event log and the error-output log are emptied every time the app launches, the crash log is kept until the television restarts (the television clears its temporary storage then), and the storage snapshot is replaced when its bounded status changes. Delete all local data removes all of it.
settings.legal.privacy.fin.retention_bod.description: Settings, account, onboarding or privacy UI: settings.legal.privacy.fin.retention_body

settings.legal.privacy.fin.uninstall_bod.value: Removing FinNative removes the application, but webOS gives an application no way to run code as it is removed, so anything kept outside the application’s own directory can survive. Your sign-in is deliberately kept there so that reinstalling does not sign you out, and so is your app language preference. Use Delete all local data BEFORE uninstalling if you want nothing of FinNative left on this television.
